```{r}
student_preferences_round_1_path <- "data/BA_01_Preferences_Students.txt"
n_topics <- 4
available_topic_ids <- 1:n_topics
n_topics_per_student <- 2
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

here::i_am("main.rmd")

```

```{r}
student_preferences_round_1 <- read_csv(
  file = here(student_preferences_round_1_path)
  )

set.seed(123)  # reproducible random fills

pref_cols <- paste0("preference_", seq_len(n_topics))

student_preferences_round_1_fixed <- student_preferences_round_1 %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # 1) pull row prefs as a list-column (this line fixes your error)
    prefs = list(c_across(all_of(pref_cols))),

    # 2) keep only valid topic IDs
    prefs = list(prefs[[1]][prefs[[1]] %in% available_topic_ids]),

    # 3) drop duplicates, keep first
    prefs = list(unique(prefs[[1]])),

    # 4) fill with remaining topics (no replacement) to reach n_topics
    prefs = list({
      remaining <- setdiff(available_topic_ids, prefs[[1]])
      c(prefs[[1]], sample(remaining, n_topics - length(prefs[[1]]), replace = FALSE))
    })
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # write back into the wide columns
  mutate(
    across(all_of(pref_cols),
      ~ map2_int(prefs, str_extract(cur_column(), "\\d+"),
                 \(vec, pos) vec[as.integer(pos)])
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-prefs)

# pivot longer
student_preferences_round_1_long <- student_preferences_round_1_fixed %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = tidyselect::all_of(paste0("preference_", seq_len(n_topics))),
    names_to = "rank",
    names_prefix = "preference_",
    values_to = "topic_id"
  )

n_students <- nrow(student_preferences_round_1_fixed)
```


```{r}
# Step 1 - Create Topic Pools

## Create long randomized list of topic ids to use as filler.
topics_filler <- unlist(replicate(n_topics_per_student, sample(available_topic_ids), simplify = FALSE))


create_topic_pool <- function(round) {
    multiplier <- n_students / n_topics
    
    if(multiplier < 1) {
      message("The case that there are more topics than students is not yet supported.")
    } else if(multiplier == 1) {
      tf <- NULL
    } else {
    n_filler <- (n_topics * ceiling(multiplier)) %% n_students
    beginning <- ((round - 1) * n_filler) + 1
    tf <- topics_filler[beginning:(beginning + n_filler - 1)]
    }
    topic_pool <- c(rep(available_topic_ids, (ceiling(multiplier)-1)), tf)
  
  # sanity check
  if(length(topic_pool) != n_students) {
    message(paste0("There is something wrong with the topic pool generation for round ", round))
  }
  return(topic_pool)
}

topic_pools <- lapply(1:n_topics_per_student, function(r) create_topic_pool(r))
```


```{r}
# Step 2 - allocate topics by random serial dictatorship
allocate_by_random_serial_dictatorship <- function(preferences,
                                                   topic_pools,
                                                   # list: one vector of topic_ids per round
                                                   seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(seed))
    set.seed(seed)
  
  # ---- Helper: coerce inputs & checks ----
  validate_prefs <- function(preferences, objects) {
    req_cols <- c("student_id", "topic_id", "rank")
    if (!all(req_cols %in% names(preferences))) {
      abort(
        "`preferences` must have columns: student_id, topic_id, rank (rank 1 = most preferred)."
      )
    }
    preferences %>%
      mutate(
        student_id = as.character(student_id),
        topic_id = as.character(topic_id),
        rank = as.integer(rank)
      ) %>%
      filter(topic_id %in% objects) %>%
      arrange(student_id, rank)
  }
  
  # Validate preferences against the union of all topics that can ever appear
  all_topic_ids <- unique(unlist(topic_pools, use.names = FALSE))
  prefs <- validate_prefs(preferences, all_topic_ids)
  
  student_ids <- unique(prefs$student_id)
  n_students  <- length(student_ids)
  n_rounds    <- length(topic_pools)
  
  # 1) Hard-fail if any round's pool size != number of students
  pool_sizes <- vapply(topic_pools, length, integer(1))
  bad_rounds <- which(pool_sizes != n_students)
  if (length(bad_rounds) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Pool size mismatch: each round must have exactly ",
      n_students,
      " topics (one per student). Offending rounds: ",
      paste0(
        sprintf("#%d (size=%d)", bad_rounds, pool_sizes[bad_rounds]),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  # Fast lookup: each student's ordered preference list (best -> worst)
  student_id_lists <- prefs %>%
    dplyr::arrange(student_id, rank) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(student_id) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(pref_list = list(topic_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tibble::deframe()
  
  # Output: rows = students, cols = rounds
  assign_mat <- matrix(
    NA_character_,
    nrow = n_students,
    ncol = n_rounds,
    dimnames = list(student_ids, paste0("topic_", seq_len(n_rounds)))
  )
  
  # Track topics already assigned to each student across rounds
  assigned_by_student <- stats::setNames(vector("list", n_students), student_ids)
  
# Remove only one occurrence of each assigned id from avail (preserves order)
available_minus_assigned <- function(avail, assigned) {
  out <- avail
  if (length(assigned)) {
    for (a in assigned) {
      i <- match(a, out)      # first occurrence
      if (!is.na(i)) out <- out[-i]  # remove just one
    }
  }
  out
}

# Helper: pick highest-ranked topic for sid from current round's available,
# excluding ANY topic the student already has (set exclusion).
first_available_for <- function(sid, available_vec) {
  # be type-consistent
  available_vec <- as.character(available_vec)

  prefs_for_s <- student_id_lists[[sid]]
  if (is.null(prefs_for_s)) return(NA_character_)

  # EXCLUDE all copies of already-assigned topics for THIS student
  available_for_student <- setdiff(available_vec, assigned_by_student[[sid]])

  # highest-ranked remaining preference
  purrr::detect(prefs_for_s, ~ .x %in% available_for_student,
                .default = NA_character_)
}

  # Debug version of the picker; prints prefs, availability filtering, and final choice
debug_first_available_for <- function(sid, available_vec) {
  sid_key <- as.character(sid)
  cat("\n=== debug_first_available_for sid:", sid_key, "===\n")

  prefs_for_s <- student_id_lists[[sid_key]]
  cat("prefs_for_s:   ", if (is.null(prefs_for_s)) "NULL" else paste(prefs_for_s, collapse = " "), "\n")
  if (is.null(prefs_for_s)) {
    cat("-> No prefs for this sid. Returning NA.\n")
    return(NA_integer_)
  }

  already <- assigned_by_student[[sid_key]]
  cat("already:       ", if (is.null(already)) "NULL" else paste(already, collapse = " "), "\n")

  cat("global avail:  ", paste(available_vec, collapse = " "), "\n")

  # Use the debug multiset subtraction so you see removals step-by-step
  available_for_student <- available_minus_assigned(
    avail = available_vec,
    assigned = if (is.null(already)) integer(0) else already
  )

  # Choose the highest-ranked preference that is still available
  cat("available_for_student:", paste(available_for_student, collapse = " "), "\n")

  # Filter prefs by availability and show the filtered list
  keep_mask <- prefs_for_s %in% available_for_student
  filtered <- prefs_for_s[keep_mask]
  cat("filtered prefs:", if (length(filtered)) paste(filtered, collapse = " ") else "(none)", "\n")

  # Take first if present, otherwise NA
  choice <- if (length(filtered)) filtered[[1]] else NA_integer_
  cat("choice:        ", ifelse(is.na(choice), "NA", as.character(choice)), "\n")
  choice
}

# Remove exactly one occurrence of a value from a vector
remove_one <- function(vec, value) {
  i <- match(value, vec)   # index of first occurrence
  if (!is.na(i)) {
    vec <- vec[-i]         # drop just that one
  }
  vec
}
  
  # 2) Process each round independently with a fresh random order
  for (r in seq_len(n_rounds)) {
    available <- topic_pools[[r]]
    order_vec <- sample(student_ids, n_students)  # new random order each round
    for (sid in order_vec) {
      # 3) Candidate set excludes already-assigned topics for THIS student only
      choice <- debug_first_available_for(sid, available)
      if (is.na(choice)) {
        # With pool size == #students and valid prefs, this shouldn't happen.
        # If it does, it means the student's ranked list doesn't contain any of the
        # round's remaining topics (after excluding already-assigned). We stop to avoid silent NAs.
        stop(
          sprintf("No assignable topic for student '%s' in round %d. ", sid, r),
          "Check that their preferences include this round's topics ",
          "beyond those already assigned in prior rounds. Another reason could be that the last remaining topic for the student was already assigned to them in the first round.",
          call. = FALSE
        )
      }
      
      assign_mat[sid, r] <- choice
      # 4) Remove the chosen topic from THIS ROUND's availability (no duplicates in the round)
      available <- remove_one(available, choice)
      # Track for this student across rounds (prevents repeats for the same student)
      assigned_by_student[[sid]] <- c(assigned_by_student[[sid]], choice)
    }
  }
  
  tibble::as_tibble(assign_mat, rownames = "student_id") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(student_id)
}

topic_allocation_round_1 <- allocate_by_random_serial_dictatorship(preferences = student_preferences_round_1_long,
                                                                   topic_pools = topic_pools,
                                                                   seed = 20250821)
```
